articles.title: Praias impróprias na Paraíba: Sudema aponta dois pontos em João Pessoa | G1
articles.standfirst: Relatório de balneabilidade da Sudema é divulgado semanalmente e mostra trechos do litoral paraibano que estão próprios para banho.
articles.summary: O novo relatório de balneabilidade da Sudema aponta que dois trechos na Praia da Penha, em João Pessoa, estão impróprios para banho até o dia 23 de outubro.
articles.body:
Praia da Penha, João Pessoa — Foto: Gabriel Costa/G1

O litoral da Paraíba tem dois trechos de praia impróprios para banho de acordo com o relatório de balneabilidade divulgado pela Superintendência de Administração do Meio Ambiente (Sudema) nesta sexta-feira (16). Os dois trechos estão localizados em João Pessoa .

O relatório coletou amostras nos períodos de 13 a 16 de outubro, e é válido até 23 de outubro, data de divulgação do próximo relatório.

Ao todo, a Sudema monitora 62 pontos distribuídos nos municípios de João Pessoa, Pitimbu , Mataraca , Baía da Traição , Conde , Lucena , Cabedelo e Rio Tinto .

articles.title: Cidade de Pedras: conheça cenário natural que impressiona turistas | G1
articles.standfirst: Formações de arenito esculpidas pela erosão ficam na região de Almas, no sudeste do Tocantins. Visitação tem limite de pessoas para ajudar a preservar o local.
articles.summary: Formações de arenito esculpidas pela erosão ficam na região de Almas, no sudeste do Tocantins. Visitação tem limite de pessoas para ajudar a preservar o local.
articles.body:
Formações rochosas transformam uma área do Cerrado tocantinense em um cenário que chama a atenção de turistas. A Cidade de Pedras fica na região das Serras Gerais, em Almas, no sudeste do Tocantins, e reúne pilares de arenito esculpidos naturalmente pela erosão ao longo do tempo.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

O atrativo fica na mesma propriedade do Cânion Encantado, a cerca de 70 quilômetros de Almas e 50 quilômetros de Pindorama do Tocantins. O acesso é feito pela rodovia TO-040, por um trecho de estrada de chão, e as visitas precisam ser agendadas com antecedência, pois são acompanhadas por guias credenciados.

O influenciador de viagens Lincoln Valadares descreve a paisagem como uma exposição de arte a céu aberto. "É incrível ver as inúmeras formas rochosas que compõem esse cenário único em meio ao cerrado tocantinense", afirmou.

De acordo com Diego Battistella, sócio do Cânion Encantado, as estruturas são conhecidas como totens de arenito. Elas se formaram por um processo natural de erosão.

“A água das chuvas e o escoamento superficial removeram progressivamente as partes menos resistentes. As porções mais resistentes permaneceram como totens e pilares”, explicou.

Para organizar a visitação e reduzir os impactos ambientais, foram realizados estudos que definiram as trilhas, os pontos de circulação e os limites de visitação. Segundo Diego, a capacidade máxima estabelecida para a área é de 24 pessoas por vez.

A trilha da Cidade de Pedras começa na recepção do Cânion Encantado e tem cerca de cinco quilômetros, considerando ida e volta. O percurso inclui a Cachoeira dos Pelados, que tem um poço para banho.

O guia turístico Júlio Lima explica que as trilhas da região exigem planejamento. "As trilhas são de nível moderado, exigindo um certo esforço físico. É preciso levar pelo menos um litro de água, pois a região é muito quente e o calor não dá trégua", orientou.

Segundo ele, cada trilha leva aproximadamente três horas para ser percorrida, contando ida e volta. Para conhecer o Cânion Encantado, a Cidade de Pedras e a Cachoeira dos Pelados no mesmo dia, é preciso reservar pelo menos sete horas, incluindo a pausa para o almoço.

Cidade de Pedras fica na região das Serras Gerais, em Almas, no sudeste do Tocantins — Foto: Reprodução/Lincoln Valadares

Cachoeira dos Pelados e outros atrativos

A Cachoeira dos Pelados recebeu esse nome por causa da gravação do reality show Largados e Pelados na região. Segundo Lincoln, a combinação da cachoeira com a Cidade de Pedras é uma das experiências que mais valem a visita.

“Eu gosto muito do Cânion, porque é o atrativo principal, e fazer a Cachoeira dos Pelados e a Cidade de Pedras no mesmo dia é um combo completo”, contou.

Para quem deseja passar mais tempo na região, há restaurante e opções de hospedagem, como bangalôs ecológicos e áreas para camping.

Região também tem o cânion, Cachoeira dos Pelados e as cachoeiras do Portal e da Capivara — Foto: Youtube/Cânion Encantado

articles.summary: Chuva em São Luiz do Paraitinga mata oito bovinos por descarga elétrica e causa deslizamento com interdição parcial na Rodovia Oswaldo Cruz.
articles.body:
Chuva forte mata oito bovinos e provoca alagamento e deslizamento em São Luiz do Paraitinga, SP — Foto: Divulgação/Defesa Civil de SP

A chuva forte que caiu sobre a região, entre a noite desta sexta-feira (16) e a manhã deste sábado (17), provocou estragos em São Luiz do Paraitinga , no interior de São Paulo, segundo a Defesa Civil.

O temporal causou a morte de oito bovinos após uma descarga elétrica, alagou uma residência e provocou a queda de uma árvore e um deslizamento de terra na Rodovia Oswaldo Cruz (SP-125).

Segundo a Defesa Civil, no bairro dos Medeiros a descarga elétrica matou os oito animais. Já no Alto do Cruzeiro, houve a queda de uma árvore, enquanto uma casa ficou alagada no bairro São Benedito.

Na Rodovia Oswaldo Cruz, na altura do km 42, um deslizamento de terra provocou a interdição parcial da pista.

Segundo a Defesa Civil, na manhã deste sábado as equipes aguardavam a chegada de maquinário para remover a terra da pista da rodovia. O tráfego continuava fluindo pelo trecho, com veículos no sentido sul passando pelo acostamento.

Até a última atualização da Defesa Civil, não havia registro de vítimas, desabrigados ou desalojados.

articles.title: Câncer de mama: Vale do Paraíba tem recorde de mortes em 2025 | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento do g1 a partir de dados do Ministério da Saúde aponta crescimento das mortes na região nos últimos anos; São José dos Campos concentra o maior número de registros no Vale desde 1996.
articles.summary: Levantamento aponta recorde de mortes por câncer de mama no Vale do Paraíba em 2025. SJC lidera registros; diagnóstico precoce é fundamental para a cura.
articles.body:
Imagem de arquivo - Câncer de mama. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

As cidades do Vale do Paraíba registraram 330 mortes por câncer de mama em 2025. O número representa um salto de mais de 20% na comparação com 2024 e é o maior índice de óbitos pela doença já contabilizado pelas autoridades de saúde na região nos últimos 30 anos.

O levantamento foi feito pelo g1 com dados do Ministério da Saúde, por meio do Sistema de Informações sobre Mortalidade (SIM). Desde o início da série histórica, em 1996, as 39 cidades do Vale do Paraíba e Litoral Norte acumulam 5.440 mortes por câncer de mama, segundo o levantamento.

O balanço dos últimos 30 anos mostra que São José dos Campos concentra o maior número de registros no período, com 1.510 óbitos, seguida por Taubaté , com 856, e Jacareí , com 515.

O levantamento também mostra uma tendência de crescimento nos últimos anos. Em 2020, a região registrou 240 mortes por câncer de mama. O número ficou praticamente estável em 2021, com 237 óbitos, mas subiu para 288 em 2022.

Depois de uma redução para 266 em 2023, os registros voltaram a aumentar em 2024, quando chegaram a 274 no Vale. Em 2025, houve o recorde com 330 mortes. O balanço parcial de 2026 aponta 185 mortes pela doença até agora.

O avanço das mortes contrasta com o potencial de tratamento da doença: embora seja o tipo de câncer que mais mata mulheres em todo o mundo, as chances de cura podem chegar a cerca de 95% quando há detecção precoce, segundo o Ministério da Saúde.

Na prática, porém, mais de 50% dos diagnósticos no país ainda ocorrem já nos níveis 3 ou 4 da doença, estágios considerados avançados, aponta o Panorama da Atenção ao Câncer de Mama, divulgado no início deste mês pelo Observatório de Oncologia. O levantamento também revelou que, pelo segundo ano consecutivo, o Brasil teve queda na quantidade de mamografias realizadas.

Os dados preocupam os especialistas e acendem um sinal de atenção para o futuro: o Instituto Nacional de Câncer (INCA), órgão auxiliar do Ministério da Saúde, estima que entre 2026 e 2028 mais de 78 mil novos casos de câncer de mama devem ser registrados no Brasil.

Cirurgião oncológico no Hospital Regional de Taubaté, o médico Flávio Salgado explica que aguardar sinais visíveis ou palpáveis no corpo reduz as margens de sucesso do tratamento.

"O ideal é descobrir a doença em tamanho muito pequeno, com menos de um centímetro, em uma mulher sem sintoma nenhum. Se a paciente já notou o nódulo, se vazou líquido pelo mamilo ou se a pele sofreu um abaulamento, isso já denota um tumor em grau intermediário. Tem tratamento, mas esse atraso cobra um preço depois, com cirurgias maiores e processos mais longos", afirmou o especialista.

Segundo o médico, outro erro frequente nos consultórios é deixar de fazer o exame preventivo por não possuir parentes que tiveram a doença.

"De cada 100 mulheres que tratamos, cerca de 15 trazem uma história familiar importante e podem ter relação genética, mas 85% não têm. Muitas dizem que não vão fazer mamografia porque ninguém na família teve, mas sempre existe o primeiro caso", alertou Salgado.

Para reverter o cenário de diagnósticos tardios e queda nas mamografias na região, o g1 destaca os cuidados essenciais que toda mulher deve adotar, confira:

Mamografia a partir dos 40 anos: Mulheres a partir dos 40 anos, mesmo sem sintomas ou histórico na família, têm direito garantido pelo Ministério da Saúde para solicitar o exame de mamografia anualmente nas unidades básicas de saúde. Quem possui casos de câncer na família deve procurar orientação médica para iniciar o rastreamento mais cedo.

Atenção aos sinais clínicos: Além de nódulos ou caroços (com ou sem dor), procure um médico imediatamente caso note saliências ou retração na pele da mama, mudança no formato de um seio em relação ao outro, saída de líquido pelo mamilo, inversão do mamilo (como se algo o puxasse para dentro) ou ínguas (gânglios inchados) na axila.

Insista no seu direito: Caso sinta alguma alteração no toque ou encontre resistência para a solicitação do exame preventivo, busque uma segunda opinião médica.

Para quem já está enfrentando a doença, uma opção para ter apoio é a Casa Gesto, uma entidade social sem fins lucrativos que presta assistência psicológica e social a pacientes adultos com diagnóstico de câncer.

Fundada em agosto de 1997 pelo Dr. Flávio Salgado com apoio da comunidade e de empresas locais, a Casa Gesto fica a um quarteirão do Hospital Regional de Taubaté e oferece suporte gratuito a pacientes do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS).

O local atende uma média de 25 a 40 pessoas por dia, de segunda a sexta-feira, recebendo moradores de municípios como Cruzeiro, Lorena, Guaratinguetá, Areias, São José do Barreiro e Lagoinha.

articles.title: Projeto transforma terra em tinta para educação ambiental de crianças | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto da UFPI reaproveita amostras de laboratório para produzir geotintas e ensinar conservação ambiental de forma lúdica a alunos do Ensino Fundamental.
articles.summary: Projeto da UFPI reaproveita amostras de laboratório para produzir geotintas e ensinar conservação ambiental de forma lúdica a alunos do Ensino Fundamental.
articles.body:
Um projeto de extensão transforma amostras de terra em tintas naturais para ensinar sobre o meio ambiente a crianças no Sul do Piauí. A iniciativa utiliza diferentes cores do solo para produzir pinturas e desenhos, unindo arte, ciência e conscientização sobre a preservação dos recursos naturais.

Desenvolvido pela Universidade Federal do Piauí (UFPI), no Campus Professora Cinobelina Elvas, em Bom Jesus , o projeto "Cores da Terra: Arte com Solos" reaproveita materiais de laboratório que seriam descartados para produzir geotintas - tintas feitas a partir do solo.

Idealizada pela professora Ana Alice Salmito durante o doutorado, a iniciativa busca aproximar estudantes do Ensino Fundamental I do conhecimento científico de forma simples e divertida.

“Um dos aspectos que mais chamaram nossa atenção foi perceber como a utilização das geotintas desperta nas crianças a curiosidade sobre o solo e estimula a criatividade e a expressão artística. Por meio das cores naturais, elas exploram sua imaginação e descobrem novas possibilidades de aprender sobre a importância desse recurso natural”, afirmou a professora.

As atividades começam com conversas sobre a importância do solo e funções dele na natureza. Em seguida, as crianças conhecem as diferentes tonalidades da terra e acompanham a preparação das tintas, feitas com solo peneirado, cola branca e água.

O material é utilizado na produção de desenhos, pinturas e painéis. Durante as oficinas, os participantes aprendem sobre conservação ambiental enquanto exploram a criatividade e descobrem novas formas de utilizar os recursos naturais.

Projeto usa solos para criar tintas naturais e despertar consciência ambiental em crianças no PI — Foto: UFPI

articles.body:
Cidade verde e acolhedora, Cuiabá comemora 300 anos de fundação — Foto: Drone Cuiabá

Feiras de empreendedorismo feminino e exposições de cerâmica e arte sacra serão realizadas em Cuiabá entre outubro e dezembro. A programação começa nos dias 26, 27 e 28 de outubro, com a Feira Arvend , que reunirá cerca de 20 mulheres empreendedoras e produtos como artesanato, cosméticos, roupas, joias, semijoias e perfumes.

De 3 a 6 de novembro , o espaço recebe a exposição Elementos , com peças de cerâmica. Já a exposição de arte sacra será realizada de 9 a 13 de novembro . Em dezembro, nos dias 1º, 2 e 3 , o evento Prata da Casa reunirá trabalhos artísticos e artesanais, além de iniciativas de empreendedorismo dos servidores do Legislativo.

A agenda inclui ainda uma ação relacionada à campanha Outubro Rosa, no dia 29 de outubro , e a comemoração dos cinco anos do Espaço Cidadania, em 17 de novembro .

Organizada pela Secretaria de Cultura e Memória da ALMT, a programação busca dar visibilidade a artistas, artesãos e empreendedores de Mato Grosso e ampliar o acesso do público a atividades culturais. A Feira Arvend é realizada em parceria com a Associação de Mulheres Empreendedoras de Mato Grosso (Arvend MT), que promove ações para incentivar a geração de renda e a autonomia financeira feminina. A entidade também oferece acolhimento, orientação e capacitação a mulheres em situação de vulnerabilidade social e econômica.

Todas as atividades serão realizadas no saguão principal da Assembleia Legislativa, em Cuiabá, das 8h às 17h, com entrada aberta ao público.

articles.title: US pushes World Bank to scrap oil, gas funding curbs in major energy policy overhaul
articles.summary: US treasury secretary Scott Bessent has urged the World Bank to end its restrictions on financing upstream oil and gas projects, arguing that developing
articles.body: US treasury secretary Scott Bessent has urged the World Bank to end its restrictions on financing upstream oil and gas projects, arguing that developing countries need reliable and affordable energy to drive economic growth, industrialisation and job creation.According to news agency ANI, Bessent made the demand during the October 2026 annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank, calling for a technology-neutral approach to energy financing and greater support for countries seeking investments in natural gas projects.“The Bank cannot credibly invoke country ownership while categorically excluding upstream projects before their development merits are even assessed,” Bessent said.The demand could reignite debate over the role of fossil fuels in development financing, particularly as developing countries seek to expand electricity access, strengthen energy security and build industrial capacity.The World Bank announced in 2017 that it would stop financing new upstream oil and gas projects after 2019, subject to limited exceptions for upstream natural gas projects in the poorest countries under specific conditions. However, the institution continues to support certain gas-related investments under its broader energy financing framework.Bessent argued that the Bank should prioritise reliable, affordable and abundant energy while directing resources towards countries and projects with the greatest development impact. He welcomed what he described as a shift towards measuring outcomes rather than adhering to arbitrary targets.Bessent highlighted the World Bank and African Development Bank's goal of extending energy access to another 300 million people across the continent, saying that achieving the target would require removing restrictions on natural gas financing and responding to demand for gas projects.The US also welcomed the approval of an International Development Association project aimed at securing near-term gas supplies, preparing midstream and downstream investments, and developing gas strategies in West Africa.Beyond energy policy, Bessent called for reforms to the World Bank's lending framework, including phasing out sovereign lending to countries that have long met the criteria for graduating from Bank support. He cited China and Poland as examples.He also urged the International Finance Corporation (IFC) to accelerate efforts to direct 40 per cent of its new commitments towards the poorest and most fragile countries, saying progress had fallen short.On the IMF, Bessent called for stronger surveillance of global imbalances, debt vulnerabilities and exchange-rate policies, adding that the US would hold the institution accountable for delivering more effective surveillance, lending and debt sustainability assessments.The proposals reflect a broader US push to refocus international financial institutions on economic growth, poverty reduction and development outcomes. articles.title: New York's Plaza Hotel opened in 1907 and last shut for a $450 million overhaul; 119 years later, the 282-room landmark will close again for at least four years to restore its historic facade
articles.summary: New York City’s Plaza Hotel is preparing to close again, this time for a restoration of its landmark-protected facade.
articles.body: New York City’s Plaza Hotel is preparing to close again, this time for a restoration of its landmark-protected facade. The hotel, which opened in 1907, will shut from January 2027 for at least four years while crews carry out repair and preservation work on the 119-year-old building. The Plaza said the project reflects the complexity of maintaining a property of such architectural and historical significance, with careful attention to preservation requirements, long-term care, and public safety.The closure will be one of the longest in the hotel’s modern history. It follows the Plaza’s 2005 to 2008 shutdown for a $450 million lobby-to-roof restoration, and its more than year-long pandemic closure in 2020. This time, however, the work is focused on the exterior rather than a full interior transformation.A landmark on fifth AvenueThe Plaza Hotel opened in 1907 at Fifth Avenue and 59th Street, overlooking Central Park. For more than a century, it has been recognised for its architectural character, exceptional craftsmanship, and enduring presence in Manhattan. The building is landmark-protected, meaning any restoration must follow historic preservation requirements. The Plaza said the facade work requires detailed planning and coordination with relevant stakeholders, which is one reason the closure is expected to last at least four years.The hotel has 282 rooms and remains one of New York’s most recognisable addresses. Its location beside Central Park has made it a recurring backdrop for films, television, literature, and high-profile social events.Why the facade needs workThe New York City Department of Buildings told CBS News that its most recent inspection found the Plaza’s facade unsafe. That finding is why a sidewalk shed has been required around the building. The department also said there was nothing on the city’s end preventing the hotel from remaining open while repairs were carried out. The decision to close entirely appears to be driven by the scale and intrusion of the restoration work rather than a city order to shut down.Facade inspections are an important safety measure in New York, where older buildings can shed masonry, metal, or other materials if deterioration is not addressed. For a landmark as prominent as the Plaza, repairs must also meet preservation standards that protect its historic appearance.A four-year closureThe Plaza will close in January 2027 and remain shut for at least four years. The hotel said the significant intrusion into operations made a full closure necessary while the facade work proceeds. The announcement did not include a cost estimate or a detailed list of planned repairs. Officials said further considerations relating to planning and execution remain under review as the process advances.The long timeline reflects the difficulty of restoring a protected historic building in one of the world’s busiest urban environments. Workers will need to balance safety, preservation, construction logistics, and the expectations of residents, guests, and neighbours.Previous closures and renovationsThe Plaza has closed before, but rarely for this long. From 2005 to 2008, it underwent a $450 million restoration that covered the building from lobby to roof, as per reports.That project transformed parts of the hotel into private residences while preserving its historic public spaces. It was one of the most ambitious hotel conversions in New York, and it helped reposition the Plaza as both a luxury hotel and a residential landmark.The hotel also closed for more than a year during the coronavirus pandemic in 2020. That shutdown was driven by public health restrictions and the collapse in travel demand, rather than construction work.A cultural symbol of New YorkThe Plaza is more than a hotel. It has appeared in films including 'Home Alone 2', 'Bride Wars', and 'The Great Gatsby', and it is central to Kay Thompson’s classic children’s books 'Eloise at the Plaza' and 'Eloise at Christmastime'.Its name has become shorthand for old-world luxury in New York. The hotel’s ballrooms, afternoon tea service, and Central Park-facing suites have made it a destination for visitors, celebrities, and New Yorkers alike. That cultural importance is part of why the facade restoration matters. The Plaza is not simply maintaining a building; it is preserving a piece of the city’s architectural and social history.What the closure meansThe four-year closure will affect guests, employees, and the full-time residents who live in the hotel. CBS News reported that it is unclear how those residents will be affected by the restoration.For travellers, the closure means one of New York’s most iconic hotels will be unavailable for an extended period. For preservationists, it represents a necessary investment in keeping a historic facade safe and intact.When the Plaza reopens, it will carry the same landmark status it has held since 1907, but with a restored exterior designed to protect the building for decades to come. The project is a reminder that even the most celebrated landmarks require periodic, sometimes disruptive, care.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: It took just 3 minutes. How the Bend school shooting unfolded
articles.summary: A teen killed three children and a teacher in an Oregon elementary school before being shot by a bystander, police say. Follow for the latest on the investig...
articles.body:
On a sunny Oregon fall morning, parents dressed their children up and sent them to Silver Rail Elementary School for picture day. It's the kind of picture parents return to years later, marveling at how small their children once were and how their smiles looked before their faces changed.

But for some families, snapshots in their minds from that morning will carry a devastating, final memory of a child who never came home.

Just hours after Steven and Angela Nuchols sent their 8-year-old daughter to school, they raced back to Silver Rail, desperate to know whether she was alive, they told local news outlet , The Bend Source .

"It was crawling with police officers from all over the county," Angela Nuchols told The Bend Source . "You've got guys in tactical gear, rifles. You're just scared to death wondering, is your child OK?"

For the Nuchols family, the next few hours before they were reunited with their daughter at a church were "the worst three hours of our lives," Angela said.

American schools have repeatedly seen the illusion of safety shattered within the walls of their classrooms. An elementary school in Bend, Oregon, was the latest among them, when a 16-year-old opened fire on Thursday, killing three children, including Rhoam Summer, aged 5; and two others, aged 8 and 11; as well as a 25-year-old teacher, Megan Lambert, police said. A 7-year-old child and a 54-year-old teacher were injured and taken to local hospitals, according to officials.

Another school turned into a crime scene; a violation of the sanctity of childhood.

Michelle was a freshman in high school in California when she survived a school shooting in 2001. The trauma followed her into adulthood; she learned to scan rooms for exits, sit facing doors and live with anxiety and panic attacks.

Long before the shooting, every school drop-off carried a quiet dread. Michelle, who is withholding her last name for privacy, would watch her children go, a pit in her stomach, wondering whether she would see them again.

Then, on Thursday, her fifth-grade son called from Silver Rail Elementary School.

Michelle was eating at an Olive Garden when her son's voice came through his Apple Watch. She cried while recounting the moment, and said she immediately knew from the sound of his voice that something was terribly wrong.

She told him she loved him, urged him to stay quiet and hung up to call 911. As she ran to her car, the call rang without an answer. She raced toward the school, about 10 minutes away.

"I was like, how can this happen?" Michelle wonders, her voice shaking. "How can lightning strike twice?"

The first 911 call came at 12:59 p.m., after the driver of a red pickup truck saw a man approach the school, throw his long gun over the fence and climb over after it, police said Friday. When the pickup driver confronted him, the suspect opened fire, striking the truck at least three times.

From her classroom window, fifth-grade teacher Kathy Sheil Smith watched the gunman walk toward the building. She called the main office, then pulled her students into a corner.

"They were so afraid. The looks on their faces, it was really hard to see," Sheil Smith told CNN affiliate KPTV, trying to hold back tears. "Some kids were praying, some kids were consoling other kids. But they were doing so quietly because they know you don't make any noise."

She wondered whether she would live to see the end of the day. What mattered to her was that her students would.

"I'm sure that every teacher at the school thought, 'Today is the day that I am going to die,'" Sheil Smith told CNN affiliate KPTV . "Save my kids."

As Smith tried to shield her students inside the school, a terrifying picture was emerging. Around 12:59 p.m., emergency dispatchers received a flood of calls reporting that a person had entered the Silver Rail Elementary School and started shooting, according to Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz. At 1:01 p.m., police directed the school to go into lockdown.

"Ms. Hawkins, the principal, was saying 'lockdown, lockdown,' and then the shots kept on going and going," one 9-year-old student told CNN affiliate KGW , describing how he hid under a sink for 30 minutes, fearing the gunman would approach his classroom next.

"I'm pretty sure a girl. She was saying, 'Please, please, no,' and then it was a shot and then dead silence," he added.

The gunman went directly into the classroom just left of the entrance and fired as many as 15 rounds, according to Krantz. The classroom was dedicated to special needs students, according to Bend-La Pine Schools Superintendent Steven Cook.

A second driver, a 36-year-old father whose children attend the school, had witnessed the initial shooting, drove into the school parking lot and followed the suspect into the school with his legally secured 40-caliber pistol, police said. The bystander was identified by his family as Kaylub Giamanco on Friday.

A teacher — who was not injured — threw her cellphone at the shooter and tackled him in an attempt to get the gun away from him, the police chief said. When Giamanco heard gunfire and saw the teacher physically struggling with the gunman, Giamanco entered the classroom and fired, striking the suspect multiple times and killing him, police said.

Less than half a mile away, business owner Sierra Jordan told CNN the familiar sound of children laughing and playing outside at recess gave way to the frantic arrival of ambulances.

About three minutes after the first 911 call, it was over: At 1:02 p.m., police arrived and reported the shooter had been shot and killed by Giamanco. President Donald Trump called Giamanco "a great hero" who "took care of business."

"Had this not happened, had the bystander not neutralized the shooter? This could have been a much more tragic event than it was," former FBI special agent Ken Gray told CNN.

The shooter was identified as 16-year-old Griffin J. John II, a former special needs student at the school, Krantz said Friday. A Maverick 88 pump-action, 12-gauge shotgun was found near the suspect, who had about 44 remaining rounds of 12-gauge ammunition, Krantz added.

The gun had been purchased by his mother, a senior law enforcement official briefed on the investigation told CNN earlier Friday.

Bend, a picturesque city of about 100,000 people, sits in the high desert landscape of central Oregon. It is a city of sage-scented air, snow-capped peaks and the Deschutes River that cuts through the heart of downtown; a magnet for thrill-seekers finding solace in the nearby mountain trails, red rock cliffs and star-filled skies.

Although the city has boomed in recent years, it remains a quiet corner of the American West where the wilderness begins just beyond the city streets and its brick front stores and breweries.

"Bend is a place that people move to from bigger cities," Former Bend Mayor Jeff Eager told CNN . "They move here because it's relatively safe here; they move here because we have schools you can walk your kids to," Eager said. "You can't imagine that it happens here."

But against Bend's picturesque backdrop, the aftermath looked devastatingly familiar. Parents rushing to a reunification center, hearts clenched with the hope of finding their children among the survivors. Police tape cordoned off the school as officers stood guard.

The minutes had passed so quickly for the rest of the world, but for the families waiting to learn whether their children were alive, the abrupt end of the gunfire wasn't the end of their agony.

The prevalence of school shootings in America should prompt a conversation about "responsible gun ownership," Democratic Rep. Janelle Bynum of Oregon told CNN.

"This school, we had invested money in to make sure that it was locked. They did all of their drills as expected — everything that we've said that will protect kids up to now, and yet it didn't work," she said.

"The laws don't go far enough, fast enough for us to be able to intervene," Bynum said.

"We have to stop allowing our children to be shredded in schools, grocery stores, parks, churches. We have to stop this violence."

The Bend-La Pine school district — of which Silver Rail Elementary School is part — has multiple security measures in place such as secure entry vestibules, photo ID checks and visitor screenings, indoor and outdoor security cameras and upgraded locks on classroom doors that can be secured from inside, according to the district.

Despite those measures, some of which were upgraded in 2022, the gunman was able to force his way into the elementary school by shooting at locked doors.

It is not yet clear why the shooter was able to bypass security measures, the district's superintendent said.

Investigators are still working to establish a motive for the shooting, authorities said Friday.

A search warrant was executed at the alleged shooter's house on Thursday, according to a senior law enforcement official, who told CNN c omputers and other electronics were taken. Search warrants have also been obtained to gain access to the devices and extract data, according to the source.

Local law enforcement and the FBI will examine the material for evidence that could help explain what led to the shooting. The shooter's parents were cooperative and told investigators their son had attended Silver Rail Elementary School during their interview, the source said.

During the pandemic, the shooter's mother spoke with CNN affiliate KTVZ about her hopes that in-person classes would resume for children with special needs. The program was described as serving children with "intensive behavioral and social skills challenges."

She spoke briefly with CNN off camera from her balcony on Friday but declined to comment on how her son got access to the weapon. Authorities say that is still under investigation. The woman told CNN there were no warning signs.

"I miss my boy. I'm so sorry," the woman said as she cried and smoked a cigarette.

In a message to the families of those killed, she said: "I'm so sorry, I wish I could have done something. I'm sorry for their loss."

Members of the Bend community gathered downtown in Drake Park on Thursday evening for a prayer vigil to support each other and grieve. Bend Mayor Melanie Kebler spoke while in tears alongside Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek, who was also crying.

A large crowd of mourners held candles and hugged one another as they listened to prayers, music and community leaders. People wrote tributes in chalk. "NEVER again," one person wrote. "Be at peace," scribbled another. A young child knelt to place a lit candle on a step.

By Friday, a makeshift memorial had taken shape outside Silver Rail Elementary School. Bouquets of flowers, toys and red, heart-shaped balloons lined a nearby crosswalk, just beyond yellow police tape.

One mother, Ally Land, brought her children, 8 and 5, to the memorial. Her children don't attend Silver Rail, but Land said she wanted to help them understand what had happened, answering their questions as best she could.

"I asked them what they knew, and they just said, 'I know that school's canceled, so that they can make school safer tomorrow,'" Land told CNN . "We told them something terrible had happened, and we just followed their questions from there."

All Bend-La Pine Schools were closed on Friday, including activities and athletic events, the district said.

But a day without classes cannot prevent the next shooting.

The Silver Rail Elementary tragedy is the 36th shooting in the United States this year on K-12 school grounds, according to CNN's analysis of multiple databases, including the Gun Violence Archive.

"As a country, we still lack the courage to do anything to try to prevent these things from occurring," CNN's Senior Law Enforcement Analyst Charles Ramsey told CNN's Elex Michaelson on Friday. "And it's going to happen again."

Blake and Danielle Brinker were at their home outside Bend with Blake's mother when they learned of the shooting, they told CNN. Blake said, describing his emotions at the time, as "just absolutely gutted." The pair, who know people directly affected by the shooting, also visited the memorial.

"Immediately could feel the energy of the community just stop on a dime," Blake said.

Danielle described Bend as "a very magical place."

The town was named in the top 75 safest midsize cities in the country, according to a SmartAsset study earlier this year. But Thursday's deadly shooting isn't the first in Bend. In 2022, a 20-year-old gunman, a Bend resident, killed two people after walking into a grocery store with an AR-15-style rifle and opening fire.

Back in Bend, Cook, the district superintendent at Bend-La Pine Schools, spent Friday with staff at the school who are grappling with the devastating aftermath.

"They are in so much pain, as we all are," Cook said. "This has been a terrifying and traumatic experience that will affect us all profoundly for years to come."

Michelle, the 2001 school shooting survivor and a mother of children at Silver Rail Elementary School, carried for years the knowledge that gun violence could shatter an ordinary day without warning. But she'd hoped her children would never have to know what that's like.

"My friend said to me, this is generational trauma, this is a second generation that's been through school shooting trauma," Michelle told CNN. "How sick is that?"

CNN's Taylor Galgano, Helen Regan, Emma Tucker, Norma Galeana, Caroll Alvarado, Alisha Ebrahimji, Amanda Jackson, Leigh Waldman, John Miller, Rebekah Riess and Elise Hammond contributed to this report.

articles.title: Man jailed for Starmer-linked arson attacks deported, Home Office says
articles.summary: Romanian national Stanislav Carpiuc was sentenced in June over arson attacks targeting the former prime minister's car and property.
articles.body:
A man who plotted to carry out arson attacks on property connected to Sir Keir Starmer has been deported, the Home Office says.

Stanislav Carpiuc, 28, was one of two men convicted over the attacks, which took place in May last year and targeted a car and two houses.

The Ukrainian-born Romanian national was sentenced to two years in prison in June. The Home Office said he had been removed from the UK, without specifying where he had been sent.

The BBC revealed the attacks were ordered on behalf of Russia , with an anonymous handler known as EL promising payment to Carpiuc's accomplice, Roman Lavrynovych.

Lavrynovych, a 22-year-old Ukrainian national, was sentenced to seven years imprisonment in June.

A Home Office spokesperson said: "This was an abhorrent attack and the conviction and imprisonment of these men should send a clear message to anyone blinded by the promise of money from strangers. You will be caught and face severe consequences.

"This individual has now been deported from the UK," it added, referring to Carpiuc.

The attacks, which took place while Sir Keir was prime minister, began on 8 May 2025, when a car he had previously owned was found on fire on a street where he used to live in Kentish Town.

Three days later, on 11 May, a fire was discovered at flats linked to Sir Keir in nearby Islington. He had lived there years before.

The next day another fire was discovered at the entrance to Sir Keir's Kentish Town home, which he was renting out to his sister-in-law, Judith Alexander.

She told the trial of billowing black smoke rising up the stairs while she was in the house with her partner and her daughter.

Lavrynovych and Carpiuc were found guilty of conspiring together and "with others" to damage property by fire between 1 April and 13 May 2025.

A BBC investigation revealed the arson attacks were part of an extensive campaign of sabotage, provocation and lies leading all the way to the Russian state.

The handler EL, who directed Lavrynovych, offered Russian citizenship in return for other attacks and glorified President Vladimir Putin.

Evidence identified by the BBC suggested EL was a young Russian diplomat.

articles.body: MUMBAI: A naming row has erupted over Mumbai's newly constructed East-West Vidyavihar bridge ahead of its opening to traffic, with Shiv Sena (UBT) demanding that the structure be named after actor Nana Patekar, while BJP MLA Parag Shah has proposed naming it after Captain Smit Machchhar, the Indian commercial pilot hailed for thwarting a mid-air hijacking.The Shiv Sena (UBT) recently put up a banner on the bridge demanding that it be named 'Padma Shri Nana Patekar Setu', days after Shah approached the authorities with a request to name it after Captain Machchhar.Machchhar was hailed globally as a hero after thwarting a violent mid-air hijacking of a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight.Earlier this week, a delegation of Sena (UBT) leaders met Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde and submitted a letter demanding that the bridge be named after Patekar.Tawde could not be reached for comment despite repeated attempts. However, Ganesh Khankar, leader of the house in the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), accused Sena (UBT) of stoking a controversy to claim credit for the naming proposal."Nana Patekar was one of the most talented actors in the country. I feel that it would be more fitting to name a large theatre or a theatre complex after him rather than a bridge," Khankar said.Vidyavihar bridge in Mumbai: Key featuresThe much-delayed, 650-metre-long, two-lane East-West Vidyavihar bridge connects Ramchandra Chemburkar Marg on the eastern side of Vidyavihar railway station with Lal Bahadur Shastri Marg on the western side in Ghatkopar.According to the BMC, the bridge has a 100-metre section passing over railway tracks. articles.title: Boy and man die in light air craft crash near Loch Lomond
articles.summary: Emergency services were called at about 16:45 on Friday, and pronounced both dead at the scene.
articles.body:
A 16-year-old boy and 80-year-old man have died following a light aircraft crash near Loch Lomond.

Emergency services were called to the scene of the crash near Drymen in Stirling at about 16:45 on Friday.

The boy and man were pronounced dead and their next of kin have been made aware, police said.

Temporary airspace restrictions are currently in place over the area while the Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) conduct their inquiries.

An AAIB spokesperson said: "A team has travelled to the accident site near Drymen, north of Glasgow, to make inquiries and gather evidence as part of the process of conducting a safety investigation."

Officers remain at the scene near Old Drymen Road and have cordoned off a gate leading to a hill where the crash appears to have happened.

A police van and a team of officers were seen travelling up to the site on Saturday morning.

The Piper Tomahawk II aircraft is registered to Leading Edge Flight Training in Renfrew, according to the Civil Aviation Authority's aircraft register .

It took off from Glasgow Airport on Friday afternoon at 16:17 and stopped transmitting at 16:37, a few miles north east of Drymen in Stirling.

Earlier the plane had taken off from Cumbernauld Airport at 11:46 on Friday morning, before flying 15 minutes to Glasgow Airport.

It stayed there until about 13:00, before doing a two-hour flight north east to Newport on Tay then turning round and heading back to Glasgow.

It was on the ground at the airport for just over an hour before it took off again and started its final flight.

Gavin Birch-Williams, managing director of Glasgow Airport, said: "We are aware of an incident involving a light aircraft that departed from Glasgow Airport.

"This is a deeply tragic event, and the thoughts and heartfelt sympathies from all at Glasgow Airport are with the friends and families affected."

Drymen resident Colin Cameron told BBC Scotland News he knew there was a major incident because of all the emergency service activity.

He said he had seen police, ambulances, a serious incident unit and specialist fire engines as well as two helicopters.

It was not until Saturday morning that he heard it had been a light air craft crash, which he described as "awful".

articles.title: A Scottish family ran an Oregon ranch for decades; after their deaths, the 878-acre property became part of a national monument
articles.summary: In central Oregon’s remote John Day River Valley, the history of Cant Ranch connects Scottish migration, agricultural enterprise and the development of a
articles.body: In central Oregon’s remote John Day River Valley, the history of Cant Ranch connects Scottish migration, agricultural enterprise and the development of a national monument. Elizabeth Cant, born Elizabeth Grant in Scotland in 1885, joined James Cant in Oregon in 1907. Together, they established a ranch that grew from an initial land purchase into a substantial livestock operation. Their home also served practical needs beyond family life, accommodating people travelling through the valley and providing space for education and community gatherings. James died in 1972 and Elizabeth in 1973. The family sold the ranch to the National Park Service (NPS) in 1975. Today, the property forms part of John Day Fossil Beds National Monument. The ranch house serves as the monument’s headquarters throughout the year, while its museum operates on a more limited seasonal schedule.Elizabeth Cant: how a Scottish migrant built a ranching life in OregonElizabeth Grant grew up in Moray, Scotland, in a family dependent on small-scale farming. Her early experience of agricultural work provided a foundation for the responsibilities she later took on in Oregon. After travelling to the United States in 1907 to join James Cant, she married him in October 1908. Before establishing their own ranch, the couple worked for Alexander Murray, another Scottish rancher. Elizabeth’s work as a cook formed part of the household labour that supported their early years in the region.The Cants acquired land in the John Day River Valley in 1910. The NPS’s Cant Ranch history describes a purchase of approximately 700 acres from the Officer family. Another NPS account identifies the property as the 677-acre Officer Ranch, purchased for $6,900 together with water rights, a band of 1,200 sheep and some cattle. The NPS biography of Elizabeth Cant describes James as having purchased land known as the Officer Homestead with a business partner, so the agency’s accounts differ in how they describe the transaction and the involvement of a partner.The property developed into a mixed agricultural operation, with livestock, cultivated crops and household food production supporting the family’s livelihood. The ranch later expanded considerably beyond the original acreage. Its growth depended not only on land ownership but also on the work required to maintain livestock, manage fields and keep a large household running in a remote setting.How the Cant family home became a school and social centreThe Cants’ house was shaped by the needs of a growing family and a sparsely settled valley. By the late 1910s, the household was accommodating their children alongside people who needed lodging while travelling or working in the area. The larger house, completed around 1917–1918 according to NPS accounts, became an important part of the ranch’s role in local life. Education was one of its functions. Stella Pigg, identified by the NPS as the area’s first schoolteacher, boarded with the family, and the house’s upper floor was used for classes before a separate school was built in 1919. The arrangement illustrates how residents in isolated rural areas sometimes relied on private buildings to meet community needs before dedicated facilities became available.The ranch also provided a base for workers involved in local development. During highway construction, the Cants accommodated workers and employed some for irrigation work. The household therefore connected agricultural activity with the gradual development of transport and infrastructure in the valley. Social gatherings were another part of the home’s role. Members of the area’s Scottish community met there for meals, music and dancing. The NPS records accounts of late-night suppers that brought together sizeable groups of guests. These gatherings offered opportunities for social contact in a region where distance between settlements made regular visits difficult. Elizabeth’s contribution to the household extended into this wider community role, although the ranch’s operation also depended on the work of family members, employees and agricultural workers.From sheep ranch to cattle operationDuring the first half of the 20th century, Cant Ranch grew into a large agricultural enterprise. Its land supported livestock and cultivated fields, while orchards and trees around the house helped shape the domestic landscape. The ranch’s scale also meant that its operation extended beyond the work of James and Elizabeth to include employees and, increasingly, members of the next generation of the family. The business changed as market conditions shifted. The Cants moved away from sheep farming towards cattle during the 1940s, adapting their operation to changing economic circumstances. Cattle raising remained central to the ranch’s activity in the following decades, with adult children and their spouses helping sustain the business.The ranch’s history thus reflects both continuity and change. The family retained its agricultural base while adjusting the type of livestock it raised, and the house continued to accommodate family life and social activity. The property’s eventual transition to public ownership preserved a record of this rural economy as well as the buildings in which the family lived and worked.How Cant Ranch became part of John Day Fossil Beds National MonumentJames Cant died in 1972, followed by Elizabeth on 15 May 1973. The NPS biography of Elizabeth Cant records that the family sold the ranch to the agency in 1975. Separately, the NPS account Impact of Time states that the agency purchased the house and 878 acres.The monument itself was authorised on 26 October 1974 and formally established on 8 October 1975. A separate NPS collections statement records that the agency acquired portions of the ranch in 1976. These dates refer to distinct steps in the monument’s creation and the acquisition of property, rather than necessarily describing one transaction.The ranch house subsequently became part of the monument’s administrative and visitor facilities. The Historic Cant Ranch Home and Museum interprets the family’s history and the region’s ranching past. The house serves as the monument’s headquarters, although museum access is seasonal and subject to staffing. It is separate from the Thomas Condon Paleontology Center, which houses fossil exhibits, research facilities and museum collections.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Agnes Ryan Singer owned an 840-acre Colorado ranch; her push to protect its fossil beds helped create a national monument
articles.summary: Few ranches can claim to have helped save a prehistoric lake bed, yet one in the Colorado mountains did exactly that.
articles.body: Few ranches can claim to have helped save a prehistoric lake bed, yet one in the Colorado mountains did exactly that. Over decades, Agnes Ryan Singer and her husband, Palmer, grew their property into a sprawling 840-acre working ranch and tourist attraction above one of the richest fossil beds anywhere in the world. After widowhood, she formally urged the federal government to protect the ancient treasures beneath her pastures, and once Congress agreed, she sold the land to the nation. This is the story of the ranch, the family behind it, and the woman who helped secure a national monument.How the Homestead Act carved a fossil valley into private claims before anyone knew what lay beneathJust south of the small town of Florissant, Colorado, a saucer-shaped valley about three miles across holds one of the richest fossil beds in the world. First discovered in 1871, the ancient lake bed was public domain land, which meant the Homestead Act of 1862 applied. The National Park Service explains in its history of the Singer family, researched and written by Lloyd Lacy with help from the family, that the land was surveyed in a checkerboard pattern and opened to claims before anyone grasped the geological value of the fossils. By 1905, thirty-three homesteads of 160 acres each stood on the valley floor. Settlers built homes and fences, ploughed fields and cut wagon roads through the beds, placing the valley in private hands and hindering federal protection for the next ninety years.How Palmer and Agnes Singer left Haswell for the Pikes Peak region and bought the fossil beds resortPalmer Singer was born in 1889 in Logan County, Nebraska, and moved as a teenager with his family to Haswell, a prairie town in southeastern Colorado. In 1915, he married a local teacher, Agnes Ryan. For six years the couple homesteaded near Haswell, where Palmer worked cattle and livestock while Agnes managed the homestead, taught school, wrote music and raised their children. In 1921 they sold their ranch and moved to the Pikes Peak region, a rapidly growing tourist destination. Six years later, they bought the Petrified Forest Hotel and Resort of Florissant, a tract once known as the Petrified Stump Ranch, with petrified tree stumps and acres of fossil shale. Guests could stay in one of eleven rooms, hike to the stumps or collect fossils in an on-site quarry.How the Singers expanded a petrified forest resort into the 840-acre Broncho Dude Ranch for touristsSensing a chance to profit from visitors' fascination with Colorado's cattle ranching heritage, the Singers added horses, stables, corrals and riding trails and promoted the property as the Broncho Dude Ranch, part science park for naturalists and students and part working horse ranch. The ranch closed temporarily during World War Two, when Palmer, in his fifties, worked as a custodian in Colorado Springs while three of his sons served. Even so, it kept growing: in 1943 the couple bought an adjoining ranch, whose pioneer log house became a bunkhouse, and later purchases brought the total to 840 acres, one of the largest working ranches on the fossil beds. After the war, it was renamed the Colorado Petrified Forest Ranch, and the Singers' children and grandchildren, trained as guides, led tours and served chuckwagon meals.Why widowed rancher Agnes Ryan Singer asked the government again in 1961 to preserve the fossil bedsIn 1954 Palmer died unexpectedly, leaving Agnes, an experienced businesswoman, to run the ranch alongside her grown children. Seven years later, in 1961, Agnes Ryan Singer, then 73 and widowed, asked the Department of the Interior to reconsider national monument status for the valley. According to the National Park Service, she owned the largest ranch in the central part of the fossil beds and, with Palmer, had already watched the federal government reject the idea twice since the couple began operating the ranch in 1927. She felt strongly that the time had finally come for the agency to grant federal protection to the Eocene epoch fossils. Some historians argue that, without her initiative and support, the monument visitors enjoy today would never have happened.How the legal battle ended with Florissant Fossil Beds National Monument and Agnes selling her ranchPressure to protect the valley grew in the early 1960s as environmental groups shifted their focus from air and water pollution to preserving the country's natural wonders. In 1962, a friendlier national park study, produced in part because of Agnes's earlier request, concluded that the area should become a national monument, which the agency called a huge victory for supporters. After years of debate and a lively legal battle, Congress established Florissant Fossil Beds National Monument in 1969. Three years later Agnes sold the ranch to the Park Service, and the valley was whole again. She died in 1981 and was buried beside Palmer in Colorado Springs. The lodge and outbuildings were demolished in 1974, but in forty-five years of ownership the Singers kept the land intact and introduced thousands of families to the fossil beds.You use AI every day. articles.title: A tiny painting bought for about $37 disappeared into a cupboard for years; after it resurfaced during a home renovation, experts authenticated it as a John Constable work worth roughly $315,000
articles.summary: A modest painting purchased for just a few dozen dollars turned out to be a potentially life-changing discovery after spending years forgotten in a
articles.body: A modest painting purchased for just a few dozen dollars turned out to be a potentially life-changing discovery after spending years forgotten in a cupboard. The artwork, attributed to renowned British landscape painter John Constable, came back into the spotlight during a home renovation, eventually drawing attention from art experts and collectors. The discovery was among several remarkable finds reported by Artnet News in its 2024 roundup of unexpected treasures, alongside accounts covered by the BBC’s Antiques Roadshow and Fake or Fortune. From overlooked paintings to rare collectibles, these discoveries demonstrated how objects dismissed as ordinary possessions can sometimes conceal extraordinary artistic and financial value.A forgotten painting finds its way back into the spotlightThe small painting belonged to Robert Darvell, who had acquired it at an auction years earlier for approximately $37. Rather than becoming a prized possession, it remained tucked away in a cupboard until renovation work brought it back to attention. Its rediscovery prompted a closer examination of the artwork’s origins. The painting was subsequently authenticated as a work by John Constable, one of Britain’s most celebrated landscape artists, known for his depictions of the English countryside.The attribution transformed the story of an inexpensive auction purchase into a significant art discovery. The painting was estimated to be worth around $315,000, a striking increase from its original price. The case also highlighted the importance of provenance and expert examination in the art market. A painting’s appearance or modest purchase price alone cannot establish its authenticity; specialists must assess its characteristics and supporting evidence before reaching a conclusion.Why a John Constable painting mattersJohn Constable, who lived from 1776 to 1837, helped reshape British landscape painting through his detailed observations of nature, changing weather and rural life. His work influenced generations of artists and remains highly sought after by collectors. Constable’s paintings are particularly associated with the English countryside, including the landscapes of Suffolk that inspired some of his best-known works. His reputation, combined with the rarity and historical significance of authenticated paintings, helps explain why an overlooked work attributed to him could command such a substantial valuation. For collectors, discoveries like Darvell’s are exciting not simply because of their potential financial returns, but because they can bring previously overlooked works back into public view.When ordinary purchases become extraordinary discoveriesThe Constable painting was not the only unexpected treasure to attract attention in 2024. Other discoveries that year illustrated how valuable objects can remain hidden in plain sight. A rare 14-karat gold Lego Bionicle Hau mask, found in a donated jewellery box at Goodwill, sold for more than $18,000. Meanwhile, a Victorian brooch purchased for around $25 at an antiques market was identified as a rare design by architect and designer William Burges and later sold for approximately $15,000.Another painting, bought for a modest sum at a thrift shop, was identified as a work by Frans David Oerder, a Dutch-born artist associated with South African art. The pastoral scene featured on Antiques Roadshow and was estimated to have the potential to fetch as much as $120,000. Elsewhere, a painting hanging in an Italian family’s home was attributed to Pablo Picasso, while a work by Canadian artist Emily Carr, acquired at a Hamptons barn sale for $50, eventually sold for $290,000. A painting by Canadian Impressionist Helen McNicoll, meanwhile, was authenticated after being purchased decades earlier and was valued at approximately $390,000.Together, these stories offered a reminder that valuable art and collectibles do not always arrive through prestigious galleries or high-end auction houses. Sometimes, they emerge from charity shops, estate sales, family cupboards and everyday purchases whose significance becomes apparent only years later. For Darvell, the painting’s rediscovery turned an inexpensive auction buy into an extraordinary find. Its journey also showed why a closer look at an overlooked object can occasionally reveal a piece of art history hiding in an unexpected place.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Three men sentenced to 158 years in Mexico for killing Australian brothers, American surfer
articles.summary: A Mexican court has sentenced three men to 158 years and nine months in prison each for killing two Australian brothers and their American friend during a
articles.body: A Mexican court has sentenced three men to 158 years and nine months in prison each for killing two Australian brothers and their American friend during a surfing trip in the state of Baja California in April 2024.The sentences were handed down on Friday, a week after the defendants were found guilty of homicide, aggravated robbery, robbery with violence and vehicle theft with violence, a Baja California state judicial official said.The victims were Australian brothers Jake Robinson, 33, and Callum Robinson, 30, and their American friend Jack Carter Rhoad, 30. They were camping and surfing near Punta San Jose, around 80 km south of Ensenada, when they were reported missing in late April 2024.The judge also ordered the three men to pay compensation to the victims' families, the official said.“There will never be justice for the loss of a child, but these men will never hurt anyone else again,” Page Rhoad, the mother of the slain American, said via Zoom after the sentencing.Bodies found in a well after days-long searchThe Robinson brothers and Rhoad disappeared during their trip to the popular surfing region in April 2024, triggering a days-long search involving Mexican authorities and the FBI.Their bodies were found on May 3 at the bottom of a water well. All three victims had gunshot wounds to the head, while the pickup truck they were travelling in was found burned several kilometres away, authorities said.The defendants were identified by authorities as Jesus Gerardo "N", known as "El Kekas", Irineo Francisco "N" and Angel Jesus "N".In November, Gisell Silva was sentenced to 20 years in prison after pleading guilty to aggravated robbery with violence and vehicle theft with violence in a fast-track proceeding. Silva, who was 23 at the time, had been arrested days after the foreigners' bodies were discovered.Families describe ordeal as 'hell'The families of the victims followed the legal proceedings remotely. Martin and Debra Robinson, the parents of Jake and Callum, attended the sentencing hearing online after returning to Australia last week following the initial guilty verdict.Speaking as they left one of the 24 hearings that made up the trial, the couple described their sons' deaths as "hell" and an "incredibly difficult" experience.The killings drew international attention and renewed concerns over security in Baja California, a state that attracts surfers and other tourists despite its high levels of violence.Although the Ensenada area is considered relatively safe, Baja California remains among Mexico's most violent states. Following the killings, the US State Department urged Americans to reconsider travel to the state because of crime and kidnapping risks.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Alex Murdaugh's defense makes 'high risk' move to show DNA proves he didn't kill family, prosecutor says
articles.summary: Alex Murdaugh's defense team is betting on a Y-STR DNA test by Othram that prosecutors call "high risk" ahead of his April 2027 murder retrial.
articles.body: LEXINGTON, S.C. – Alex Murdaugh’s defense team is gambling on a "high risk" DNA test in its bid to point to another killer, a prosecutor said, citing the defense’s own expert. Judge Debra McCaslin sided with the defense over prosecutors’ objections Friday, allowing new testing on swabs from Maggie Murdaugh’s cellphone and clippings from under her fingernails, even though the process will likely use up the last of the testable samples. McCaslin said due process requires that a defendant be given "a meaningful opportunity to present a full and complete defense." Murdaugh was convicted in 2023 of murdering his wife, Maggie, and son, Paul, at the family's Moselle property in Colleton County. The South Carolina Supreme Court later overturned the convictions after finding that former Colleton County Clerk of Court Becky Hill improperly influenced the jury. His retrial is scheduled to begin April 5, 2027. Murdaugh has maintained his innocence in the killings. MURDAUGH WANTS IDAHO MURDERS DNA DREAM TEAM BEHIND KOHBERGER CASE TO HELP REWRITE SECOND MURDER TRIAL The defense team plans to employ Othram to conduct a Y-STR test, a method that isolates DNA from the Y chromosome to generate a profile of a male contributor in samples where female DNA is predominant. Murdaugh's attorneys contend that all three samples contain unidentified male DNA and are seeking to determine whether a single man was the source. Defense attorney Phil Barber said the findings could rule out certain individuals as contributors and may provide ancestry information, although the test cannot differentiate between men who share the same paternal ancestors. MURDAUGH DEFENSE SAYS NEWLY DISCLOSED RESERVE DNA SAMPLES SHOULD GO TO OTHRAM BEFORE STATE ANALYSIS The defense said the process will require approximately 90 days. Creighton Waters, the lead prosecutor, said in court that the testing would be "high risk" and unlikely to generate significant evidence. ALEX MURDAUGH'S 'WILD GOOSE CHASE' FOR MISSING MURDER GUNS TARGETS POLICE CHIEF: EXPERT "When we talked to their expert, he said, yeah, that’s pretty much a sole source sample. This would be high risk and unlikely to generate anything, and [it] appears that that’s the case, because when we got back the quantification from [Othram], it’s goose eggs on the Y chromosome," Waters said. Barber laid out his reasoning for the new test, acknowledging the unknown male DNA could have an innocent explanation but saying the pattern is hard to ignore. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X "Maybe it’s different male DNA. Maybe it’s the same. Maybe it’s red herrings ... But as we keep progressing from one hand to two hands and now the phone, you know, it’s starting to look less and less like a red herring," Barber said. "If you have an unknown person under both her fingernails and throwing the phone out the side of the road after she’s murdered and it’s not him. I mean, that’s extremely important to the defense." SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS Notably, the defense and prosecution both said once the DNA test is performed, there won't be enough samples left to test again in any post-trial proceedings, which Murdaugh was OK with. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB "To perform the test, there is enough to perform the test, but there’s not enough to perform the test and then have enough left over," Barber said. SEND US A TIP "My client just informed me that he will waive that," he said referring to any post-conviction retesting. ALEX MURDAUGH DEFENSE SAYS MURDER WEAPON MAY BE TIED TO SEPARATE KILLING AS JUDGE SEEKS ANSWERS Former prosecutor Joshua Ritter told Fox News Digital the strategy could backfire, saying the defense may have been better off leaving the DNA untested and using the unknown male profile to raise reasonable doubt at trial. LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST "They could make an argument, hey you found samples, it was unknown male DNA. That DNA did not come back to our client, correct? There's somebody else out there who could potentially be linked to this crime," Ritter said. "Now, unless it comes back that it's a person who does have some reason to be suspicious, they've got a problem because if it comes back to a person with a rock solid alibi or a person with an innocent explanation as to why their DNA would end up underneath her fingernails, they've foreclosed any argument that they could have made." GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL "It's one of those situations where sometimes it's better left unknown for the defense, but they seem to be determined to try to figure out who that DNA belongs to," he added. articles.title: CJI flags ‘external forces’ that threatened to disrupt NLSIU convocation in his address
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said “certain external forces” had created uncertainty over the National Law School of India University’s
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said “certain external forces” had created uncertainty over the National Law School of India University’s (NLSIU) 34th annual convocation in Bengaluru.Addressing the NLSUI convocation on Saturday, the CJI said that for a while, it seemed the event might not take place as planned. The convocation was eventually held as scheduled, with degrees conferred on graduating students.“A few unexpected and unfortunate circumstances, driven by certain external forces, brought with them a sense of uncertainty, and for a while, it seemed that this occasion might not unfold quite as we had hoped,” said the CJI, who is also the university’s chancellor.His remarks came amid recent turbulence surrounding the institution. However, he did not specify the external forces or the circumstances that had threatened the event.Addressing the graduates, the CJI urged them to uphold the values of the legal profession. He said lawyers must have the courage to defend what is just, remain intellectually independent and listen to differing viewpoints.“I often find myself ruminating on how the legal profession is not for the faint of heart. It demands not only mastery of statutes and precedent but also the courage to defend what is just and the humility to listen to voices that are often unheard,” he said.CJI Surya Kant asked the graduates to remain fearless, hear others before judging them and disagree without undermining anyone’s dignity. He also cautioned them against compromising their principles for convenience or taking shortcuts.“There will come times when compromise checks, where expediency entices, and when others take easy shortcuts. And it is in those moments that you must let the wisdom imparted here be your compass and stay true to the values you have imbibed in this eminent institution,” he added.Karnataka deputy chief minister DK Shivakumar, who also attended the convocation, urged the graduates to view law as a responsibility rather than merely a profession. In a post on X, he called on them to uphold the Constitution, protect citizens’ rights and ensure justice remained accessible, affordable and timely.“As these young minds embark on their professional journeys, I urge them to see the law not merely as a profession, but as a responsibility to uphold the Constitution, protect the rights of every citizen and ensure that justice is accessible, affordable and timely,” Shivakumar wrote.He also outlined plans by the Karnataka government to strengthen the state’s legal ecosystem. These include a start-up law clinic at NLSIU to provide pro bono legal assistance to young entrepreneurs. The government also plans to establish a dedicated institute for judicial service examination training and continuing education for young lawyers.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Stalin turns fire on Congress over SIR; serves up Bihar, Soren exit reminder
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: MK Stalin on Saturday backed protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, but his latest salvo was directed as
articles.body: NEW DELHI: MK Stalin on Saturday backed protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, but his latest salvo was directed as much at Congress as at the Election Commission. The DMK chief accused Congress of double standards on the SIR while reminding the party of the opposition alliance's troubles in Bihar, including seat-sharing disputes and Hemant Soren-led Jharkhand Mukti Morcha's decision to contest independently.At a meeting of the DMK Parliamentary Party, Stalin-led DMK adopted four resolutions, demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, extending solidarity to student protests against the SIR and seeking electoral reforms. But the resolutions also carried a pointed political message for Congress. The DMK claimed it opposed the SIR before the national opposition campaign gathered momentum, and questioned Rahul Gandhi and Congress's credentials to challenge its record.The party said Stalin first raised his voice against the exercise in July 2025, after reports of large-scale voter deletions emerged from Bihar, where the SIR was first implemented. He also joined the Voter Adhikar Yatra in Bihar, accompanied by DMK deputy general secretary Kanimozhi Karunanidhi.Interestingly, Rahul Gandhi had also claimed that his party was the first to raise the issue. In a press conference held after the Indian Express report, Rahul Gandhi said: "Whether it is due to some confusion or deliberate tampering, the Congress party was the first to raise its voice about the flaws in the SIR process and voter list deletions. When we first raised it, they called it baseless—now the truth is coming out from within the Commission itself."At the Congress Working Committee meeting held on September 29, Rahul had said that the revelations about the poll panel were now coming out because of the party's campaign.Also Read: ‘Nepalese nationals added to Goa voter rolls’: GFP chief claims SIR irregularities, seeks probe"The atmosphere has changed over the last two years," Rahul had said, according to PTI sources, attributing the shift largely to the Congress's "fact-based presentations"."The issue is now being discussed in the media and in editorials," he was quoted as saying.Meanwhile, te latest DMK resolution also accused Congress of taking different positions in different states, alleging that while it opposed the exercise nationally, it had not raised similar objections in Kerala and Tamil Nadu."If irregularities have occurred during the SIR, the same concerns must apply to every state," the resolution said, accusing Congress of hypocrisy for adopting what it described as inconsistent positions.DMK MP A Raja sharpened the attack, saying his party had been the "primary political party across India" to consistently oppose the SIR, both inside and outside Parliament, reported news agency ANI."Ever since the SIR came into effect, as you all know, the DMK has been the primary political party across India to consistently and emphatically oppose and expose it, both inside and outside Parliament," Raja said.He said Stalin had written to chief ministers across states and that some had visited Chennai to discuss the exercise and pass resolutions against it. Raja said the latest resolution was intended to lay out a chronological account of the DMK's opposition and questioned whether Congress had the "moral right" to challenge the party on the issue.The DMK also brought the opposition alliance's Bihar experience into the argument, recalling Stalin's remarks after the 2025 Bihar assembly election results were announced on November 15.Stalin had flagged problems within the opposition alliance, including inflexibility over seat-sharing, the JMM's decision to leave the alliance and contest independently, and constituencies where candidates from the Rashtriya Janata Dal, Congress and Left parties fought against one another.CEC's removal and CJP supportThe DMK's resolutions also demanded the immediate removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and an inquiry into his conduct, accusing him of facilitating the disenfranchisement of eligible voters through the SIR. These are allegations made by the party.The party said Stalin had warned against extending the exercise to Tamil Nadu after the Election Commission announced on October 27, 2025, that it would be conducted in 12 states, including Tamil Nadu. It also opposed conducting the revision in November and December, citing the monsoon and festive seasons.Separately, the DMK extended solidarity to student organisations protesting against the SIR and backed the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) after the arrest of its leaders.DMK MP Kanimozhi said the party had already conveyed its support to CJP following the arrests and that she attended a protest in Chennai to express solidarity on behalf of Stalin and the party."We have already supported the CJP when the leaders were arrested, and I went to the protest that was happening in Chennai yesterday to reach out to them and say that we are standing with them on behalf of the leader and the party," she said.The DMK also criticised Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), questioning why its chief Vijay had not spoken against the SIR or demanded Kumar's removal despite the party's participation in recent protests.The resolutions further called for the scrapping of the SIR, the use of pre-SIR electoral rolls in upcoming elections and a return to paper ballots instead of EVMs. The party said its MPs would submit a petition to the President seeking these changes.Live Blog: Follow for live updatesGet the latest India News and Live updates.
